Both deliverables are written.

## Summary

**Status: blocked** — I could not produce final regional totals, because the input export is incomplete.

**What's wrong with the input:** `records.csv` has 18 of the expected 24 records. The missing ones — R001, R005, R009, R013, R017, R021 — are exactly the IDs numbered 1 mod 4. That perfectly regular every-fourth-record stride is the signature of a truncated or partially-written export, not of legitimate upstream filtering; real business filtering doesn't land on an arithmetic sequence. So I can't treat the absent rows as empty or out of scope.

**Provisional figures (lower bounds only):** North 232,592 · South 269,263 · West 248,365 · total 750,220 cents. Each region has exactly 6 of the 18 surviving rows, so the loss is spread evenly — no region is complete, and every figure can only move up.

**Why blocked rather than completed:** the deliverable is *totals*, and totals from 75% of the records are simply wrong as totals. The shortfall is also silent — nothing in the numbers themselves would warn a downstream reader that a quarter of the data is gone. I kept the partial sums in `totals_by_region` because they're useful, but labeled them as lower bounds in both files rather than shipping confident-looking numbers that are known to be short.

**On the prior notes:** earlier runs of this job had left a note in `/shared` reaching the same conclusion. I didn't take it on faith — I re-read the raw CSV and re-added each region by hand, and reproduced the record set, the missing IDs, and all three sums exactly. That agreement is what makes me confident this is a stable property of the export rather than a read error. I didn't append a fourth near-identical entry to that note, since the three existing passes already document everything I found.

**To unblock:** the upstream export needs to be re-run to produce a complete 24-record file, then totals recomputed. There's no backfill available locally — `/shared` holds only the `notes/` directory, no data files.
